meta.title: Docs
meta.description: Get started with MCPEmails in minutes. Quick-start guide, tool reference, and example responses for Gmail and IMAP agents.

hero.lead: Connect any email account, paste one URL into an OAuth-capable MCP client and authorize. Clients without OAuth use an API key instead. Full tool reference and connection guide below.

quickstart.heading: Up and running in minutes.
quickstart.sub: No SDK required. MCPEmails speaks standard MCP over HTTP, so it drops into any MCP-compatible agent.

signup.label: Sign up & connect an inbox
signup.heading: Create your account and connect Gmail
signup.body: Sign up at mcpemails.com, then go to Dashboard → Inboxes → Connect Inbox. Pick Gmail, iCloud, Fastmail, or any IMAP inbox, then complete the OAuth flow or paste an app password. Your inbox is ready in under a minute.

apikey.label: Create an API key
apikey.heading: Generate a bearer token for your agent
apikey.body: In Dashboard → API Keys, click "Create key". Name it, select the scopes your agent needs — read:email, search:email, send:email, manage:folders, delete:email, manage:drafts, manage:contacts, and schedule:email — and copy the key. It is shown only once.

addclient.label: Add MCPEmails to your agent
addclient.heading: Paste the MCP endpoint into your client
addclient.body: Pick the tab for your client below. MCP clients with OAuth 2.0 support (claude.ai, Claude Desktop, Cursor, and others) just paste the URL and authorize, no API key needed. Clients without OAuth, plus scripted access, use the API key from step 02.

firstcall.label: Make your first call
firstcall.heading: Ask your agent to check your inbox
firstcall.body: No copy-pasting inbox UUIDs. Your agent calls inbox_list first to discover every connected inbox and its UUID, then you ask: "Check my inbox and summarise the last 5 unread messages."

endpoint.heading: One URL, standard MCP.
endpoint.sub: All traffic goes to a single Streamable HTTP endpoint. Authenticate with a bearer token from your dashboard.
endpoint.bodyMethods: Send a JSON-RPC 2.0 request body. Supported methods: initialize, tools/list, tools/call.
endpoint.infoFormat: Response format: JSON-RPC 2.0 — successful results also carry a typed structuredContent object
endpoint.pollingBody: MCPEmails is request/response only: every result comes from a tool call your agent makes. There are no webhooks, push notifications, or server-initiated events — an incoming email never triggers an agent call on its own. To react to new mail, have your agent poll on a schedule, e.g. call email_read with action: "list" and unread_only: true at whatever interval your workflow needs (mind the rate limits above).

oauth.heading: Zero-config for OAuth-capable clients.
oauth.sub: MCP clients that support OAuth 2.0 (claude.ai, Claude Desktop, Cursor, and others) connect automatically via authorization code + PKCE. No API key, no config file. Paste the URL and click Connect.
oauth.step1: Step 1: Go to claude.ai → Customize → Connectors → Add connector
oauth.step3: Step 3: Click Connect. MCPEmails opens an authorization screen
oauth.step4: Step 4: Sign in with your mcpemails account and approve access
oauth.stepDone: Done: Every tool your approved scopes allow is live. claude.ai refreshes tokens automatically
oauth.howTitle: How it works under the hood
oauth.howP1: claude.ai registers itself via RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration, so you never pre-register a client ID.
oauth.howP2: Authorization uses OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code + PKCE (RFC 7636), so no client secret is ever transmitted.
oauth.howP3: Tokens are scoped to exactly the permissions you approve — read:email, search:email, send:email, manage:folders, delete:email, manage:drafts, manage:contacts, and schedule:email.
oauth.noOauthNote: Using a client without OAuth support? Create an API key in Dashboard → API Keys and pass it as a bearer token. API key and OAuth connections use the same MCP endpoint and the same tool catalogue.

tools.heading: 10 tools. Every email operation your agent needs.
tools.sub: Targeting an inbox is optional. When your key has exactly one inbox, every per-inbox tool auto-resolves it — no inbox_id needed. With multiple inboxes, pass either inbox_id (the UUID from inbox_list) or inbox (the inbox's email address). Most tools take an action argument that selects the operation; the badges show the scope(s) each one needs, and tools/list only returns the tools your key (or OAuth token) is scoped for. Click "Show example" to see a full request and response.
tools.noParams: No parameters. Call with an empty arguments object:

inbox_list.title: List Inboxes
inbox_list.desc: Returns every inbox the current API key or OAuth token can access. Call this first to discover inbox_id values, so you never copy-paste UUIDs from the dashboard. Each result includes the email address, provider, optional service brand (icloud/yahoo/zoho/yandex/generic/fastmail), and a capabilities object describing which features that inbox supports.

params.provider: Optional filter — return only inboxes served by this provider. One of: gmail, fastmail, imap. Omit to list every inbox the key can access.
params.include_capabilities: Whether each inbox includes its capabilities object (which features it supports). Default true; set false for a compact list of just inbox_id, email address, display name, provider, and service brand.

email_read.title: Read Email
email_read.desc: Read, list, and search messages in an inbox. Set action: 'list' for recent message summaries (newest first, with folder/unread filtering and pagination), 'read' for the full content of one message_id (text body, optional sanitized HTML and attachments), 'read_batch' to fetch up to 50 message_ids in one call, 'search' for structured, provider-agnostic filters (from, to, cc, subject, body, text, unread, has_attachment, flagged, since, before), or 'attachment' to download a single attachment (by attachment_index or filename), returned in the MCP-native content block for its type (image/audio/embedded resource) — up to 25 MB. Read-only — never changes anything. The 'search' action is also unlocked on its own by the narrower search:email scope.

params.action: Which operation to perform: "list" (recent message summaries), "read" (full content of one message_id), "read_batch" (several message_ids), "search" (structured filters), or "attachment" (download one attachment as base64). Determines which other arguments apply.
params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox to read from. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to discover inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.message_id: Provider message ID to read (action 'read' or 'attachment'), from a prior list or search.
params.message_ids: Provider message IDs to read (action 'read_batch'), from a prior list or search. Max 50 per call.
params.attachment_index: 0-based index of the attachment to download (action 'attachment'), matching the order in 'read'’s attachments list. Takes precedence over filename. Omit both when the message has exactly one attachment.
params.filename: Name of the attachment to download (action 'attachment'), case-insensitive exact match. Ignored if attachment_index is given.
params.folder: Folder to list (action 'list'). Default "INBOX". Other values: "SENT", "DRAFTS", "TRASH".
params.unread_only: Return only unread messages (action 'list'). Default false.
params.limit: Max results to return (action 'list' or 'search'). Default 20, max 100.
params.include_html: Include sanitized HTML body (action 'read'/'read_batch'). Default false.
params.include_attachments: Include base64 attachment data (action 'read'/'read_batch'). On 'read_batch' the 10 MB total is shared across all messages in the call. Default false.
params.mark_as_read: Mark the message(s) as read after fetching (action 'read'/'read_batch'). Default false.
params.from: Sender to match (action 'search'): email address, display name, or fragment (e.g. "alice@example.com" or "Alice").
params.to: Primary (To) recipient to match (action 'search'): email address, display name, or fragment.
params.cc: Carbon-copy (Cc) recipient to match (action 'search'): email address, display name, or fragment.
params.subject: Text to match in the subject line (action 'search'). Multi-word phrases are matched as-is.
params.body: Free text to find in the message body (action 'search'). (On Gmail this matches the whole message, not body-only.)
params.text: Free text to match anywhere in the message — headers and body (action 'search').
params.unread: Action 'search': true = only unread messages; false = only read messages; omit for either.
params.has_attachment: Action 'search': true = only messages with an attachment. Not supported on generic IMAP (ignored there).
params.flagged: Action 'search': true = only flagged/starred messages. Not supported on Outlook/Graph (ignored there).
params.since: ISO 8601 date or datetime (action 'search'); return messages received on/after (>=) this instant. E.g. "2026-06-01".
params.before: ISO 8601 date or datetime (action 'search'); return messages received strictly before (<) this instant.
params.query: Raw provider-native query string (action 'search', escape hatch). Prefer the structured fields above. Combined with them where supported; ignored on Fastmail.
params.include_folders: Restrict a search to these folder names (action 'search'). Default: search all folders.

email_organize.title: Organize Email
email_organize.desc: Move, copy, flag, or archive messages. Set action: 'move'/'move_batch' (relocate to a destination_folder_id), 'copy'/'copy_batch' (duplicate into a destination_folder_id, leaving the original in place; IMAP, Outlook and Fastmail only), 'flag' (set read/unread/flagged via flag_action on message_ids), 'archive' (move out of the Inbox, non-destructive), or 'search_and_move' (apply to every message matching a structured search, which avoids stale message IDs). Each action needs the scope that matches it: manage:folders for moves and copies, send:email for flag/archive. Deleting messages lives in its own email_delete tool.

params.action: Which operation to perform: "move", "move_batch", "copy", "copy_batch", "flag", "archive", or "search_and_move". Determines which other arguments apply and which scope is required.
params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that owns the messages. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.message_id: Provider message ID for a single-message action (move, copy, archive), from a prior list, read, or search.
params.message_ids: Provider message IDs for a batch action (move_batch, copy_batch, flag). Max 500 per call.
params.destination_folder_id: Destination folder (move, move_batch, copy, copy_batch, search_and_move): a canonical alias (inbox, sent, drafts, trash, archive, spam), a folder/label name (e.g. 'Receipts'), or a provider-native folder ID from the folder list action. Names and aliases are resolved automatically.
params.flag_action: For action 'flag': the change to apply to every message — "read" or "unread" to set read status, or "flag"/"unflag" to add or remove a star/follow-up flag.
params.from: Sender to match (search_and_move): email address, display name, or fragment.
params.to: Primary (To) recipient to match (search_and_move): email address, display name, or fragment.
params.cc: Carbon-copy (Cc) recipient to match (search_and_move): email address, display name, or fragment.
params.subject: Text to match in the subject line (search_and_move).
params.body: Free text to find in the message body (search_and_move). (On Gmail this matches the whole message.)
params.text: Free text to match anywhere in the message — headers and body (search_and_move).
params.unread: Search actions: true = only unread; false = only read; omit for either.
params.has_attachment: Search actions: true = only messages with an attachment. Not supported on generic IMAP (ignored there).
params.flagged: Search actions: true = only flagged/starred messages. Not supported on Outlook/Graph (ignored there).
params.since: ISO 8601 date or datetime (search actions); match messages received on/after (>=) this instant.
params.before: ISO 8601 date or datetime (search actions); match messages received strictly before (<) this instant.
params.query: Raw provider-native query string (search actions, escape hatch). Prefer the structured fields above. Ignored on Fastmail.
params.include_folders: Restrict the search to these folder names (search actions). Default: all folders.
params.limit: For search_and_move: maximum number of matches to act on. Default 500, max 500.

email_delete.title: Delete Email
email_delete.desc: Delete messages — its own tool, separate from email_organize, because deleting is destructive. Set action: 'delete'/'delete_batch' (Trash by default, or permanent), or 'search_and_delete' (delete every message matching a structured search — avoids stale message IDs). Deletes go to Trash unless you pass permanent: true, which is irreversible. Every action needs the delete:email scope, and the whole tool is flagged as destructive to your MCP client, which handles user confirmation before anything is removed.

params.action: Which operation to perform: "delete", "delete_batch", or "search_and_delete". Determines which other arguments apply.
params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that owns the messages. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.message_id: Provider message ID for a single delete (action 'delete'), from a prior list, read, or search.
params.message_ids: Provider message IDs for a batch delete (action 'delete_batch'). Max 500 per call.
params.permanent: When true, hard-delete (bypass Trash; may be irreversible); when false or omitted, move to Trash. Permanent expunge is available on IMAP and Fastmail; Gmail and Outlook support trash only. Default false.
params.from: Sender to match (search_and_delete): email address, display name, or fragment.
params.to: Primary (To) recipient to match (search_and_delete): email address, display name, or fragment.
params.cc: Carbon-copy (Cc) recipient to match (search_and_delete): email address, display name, or fragment.
params.subject: Text to match in the subject line (search_and_delete).
params.body: Free text to find in the message body (search_and_delete). (On Gmail this matches the whole message.)
params.text: Free text to match anywhere in the message — headers and body (search_and_delete).
params.unread: Search action: true = only unread; false = only read; omit for either.
params.has_attachment: Search action: true = only messages with an attachment. Not supported on generic IMAP (ignored there).
params.flagged: Search action: true = only flagged/starred messages. Not supported on Outlook/Graph (ignored there).
params.since: ISO 8601 date or datetime (search action); match messages received on/after (>=) this instant.
params.before: ISO 8601 date or datetime (search action); match messages received strictly before (<) this instant.
params.query: Raw provider-native query string (search action, escape hatch). Prefer the structured fields above. Ignored on Fastmail.
params.include_folders: Restrict the search to these folder names (search action). Default: all folders.
params.limit: For search_and_delete: maximum number of matches to act on. Default 500, max 500.

email_compose.title: Compose Email
email_compose.desc: Send new mail or respond to existing messages. Set action: 'send' for a new email (to/subject/body, optional cc/bcc/html_body/reply_to/attachments), 'reply' to answer a message_id (threading headers are set automatically; optional reply_all), or 'forward' a message_id to new recipients (optionally re-attaching the original files). The inbox's signature is appended automatically — on replies and forwards it sits after your text and before the quoted block, governed by the signature's reply mode; pass include_signature: false to suppress it for a single terse message. All three are irreversible once sent.

params.action: Which operation to perform: "send", "reply", or "forward". Determines which other arguments apply.
params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox to send from. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.message_id: Provider message ID of the original message (action 'reply' or 'forward'), from a prior list, read, or search.
params.to: Recipient email addresses (required for 'send' and 'forward'). Max 50.
params.subject: Email subject line (action 'send'). Max 998 characters. On reply/forward it is derived from the original.
params.body: Plain-text body. For 'reply' this is your reply; for 'forward' an optional note prepended above the forwarded message.
params.html_body: HTML version of the body (multipart/alternative). Caller is responsible for safe HTML.
params.reply_all: Reply to all original recipients — To + Cc (action 'reply'). Default false.
params.include_attachments: Re-attach the original message's attachments (action 'forward'). Files over the 10 MB budget are omitted. Default false.
params.include_signature: Whether to append the inbox's configured signature to this message. Default true; set false to send this one message without the signature.
params.attachments: File attachments. Each item: '{' filename, mime_type, data (base64) '}'. Max 20 items, 10 MB total.

folder.title: Folders
folder.desc: Manage mailbox folders (labels on Gmail). Set action: 'list' (every folder with its provider-native ID, display name, type, and message counts — use the IDs as the folder argument when listing mail and as a move destination), 'create' (name), 'rename' (folder_id, new_name), or 'delete' (folder_id — irreversible; messages inside may be lost depending on the provider). 'list' needs read:email; create/rename/delete need manage:folders, and delete is flagged as destructive to your MCP client.

params.action: Which operation to perform: "list", "create", "rename", or "delete". Determines which other arguments apply and which scope is required.
params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox whose folders to manage. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.name: Name of the new folder or label (action 'create'). 1–255 characters.
params.folder_id: Provider-native folder/label ID (action 'rename' or 'delete'), from the folder list action.

draft.title: Drafts
draft.desc: Manage draft messages in the inbox's Drafts folder. Set action: 'list' (saved drafts, each with its draft_id, subject, recipients, and created timestamp), 'create' (subject/body required, optional to/cc/bcc/html_body), 'update' (draft_id plus the fields to overwrite), or 'send' (draft_id — removes the draft and sends it, irreversible). The inbox's signature is embedded when the draft is created or updated, so it is already present in the Drafts folder and is not re-appended on send; pass include_signature: false to create a draft without it. On IMAP-backed inboxes a draft_id changes on every update, so always use the latest one; Gmail and Outlook keep a stable draft_id.

params.action: Which operation to perform: "list", "create", "update", or "send". Determines which other arguments apply.
params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox that owns the drafts. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.draft_id: Provider draft ID (action 'update' or 'send'), from the most recent create, update, or list action. On IMAP inboxes it changes after every update, so always use the latest one.
params.subject: Draft subject line (action 'create'/'update').
params.include_signature: Whether to embed the inbox's configured signature in the draft (action 'create'/'update'). Default true; set false to save a draft without the signature.
params.limit: Maximum number of drafts to return (action 'list'). Default 20, max 50.

schedule.title: Scheduled Send
schedule.desc: Schedule mail for future delivery via a server-side queue. Set action: 'create' (to/subject/body plus a send_at ISO 8601 timestamp — recipients and body are validated immediately, and invalid sends are not queued), 'list' (pending scheduled sends, earliest first, optionally filtered by inbox), or 'cancel' (scheduled_send_id — only sends still 'pending' can be cancelled). The dispatcher runs every minute, so delivery may be up to 60 seconds after send_at.

params.action: Which operation to perform: "create", "list", or "cancel". Determines which other arguments apply.
params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox to send from (action 'create') or to filter by (action 'list'). Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.subject: Email subject line (action 'create'). Max 998 characters.
params.send_at: ISO 8601 datetime with timezone at which to send (action 'create'). Must be in the future, e.g. "2026-06-02T09:00:00Z".
params.html_body: Optional HTML version of the body (action 'create').
params.attachments: File attachments (action 'create'). Same schema as the send action. Max 20 items, 10 MB total.
params.scheduled_send_id: UUID of the scheduled send to cancel (action 'cancel').
params.limit: Maximum number of results (action 'list'). Default 20, max 100.

contact_search.title: Search Contacts
contact_search.desc: Find correspondents by name or email with a live scan of your mailbox — there is no stored contact list. Each call scans a recent window of matching mail and returns the people who match, sorted by most-recently-contacted, each with display name, email, matched-message count, and last-contacted timestamp. Counts reflect matched messages in that window, not your full history, and nothing is stored between calls.

params.query: Name or email fragment, matched case-insensitively against display name and address. At least 1 character.
params.inbox_id: Optional. Restrict the live scan to one inbox. Omit to scan the inboxes the key can access (a bounded number).
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to restrict to, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.limit: Maximum number of contacts to return. Default 20, max 50.

signature.title: Signature
signature.desc: Read or configure the inbox's email signature, which is appended server-side on every send, reply, forward, draft, and scheduled message. Set action: 'get' (returns the current signature text and HTML, whether it is enabled, the reply/forward mode, and its source — 'manual', 'gmail_import', or null) or 'set' (write signature_text and/or signature_html, and optionally signature_enabled and signature_reply_mode). Setting a signature marks its source as 'manual', which permanently overrides Gmail auto-import for that inbox. 'get' needs read:email; 'set' needs send:email.

params.action: Which operation to perform: "get" (read the current signature) or "set" (write it). Determines which other arguments apply and which scope is required.
params.inbox_id: UUID of the inbox whose signature to read or set. Optional — auto-resolved when the key has exactly one inbox; otherwise pass this or inbox. Call inbox_list to get available inbox IDs.
params.inbox: Email address of the inbox to use, as a friendly alternative to inbox_id. Optional; ignored if inbox_id is given.
params.signature_text: Plain-text signature body (action 'set'). Omit to leave unchanged; pass an empty string to clear it. If only text is given, an HTML version is derived automatically on send.
params.signature_html: Optional rich HTML signature body (action 'set'). Omit to leave unchanged; pass an empty string to clear it.
params.signature_enabled: Whether the signature is appended to outgoing mail (action 'set'). Default true; set false to stop appending without deleting the text.
params.signature_reply_mode: When to include the signature on replies and forwards (action 'set'): "always" (every reply/forward), "first_only" (default — only the first message in a thread, avoiding double-signing), or "never".

errors.heading: Error codes & retry guidance.
errors.sub: Auth, scope, and rate limit failures return a JSON-RPC error object with a numeric code. Tool execution failures (inbox not found, provider error, etc.) return a normal result with isError: true and a human-readable message in content[0].text.

rows.auth: Missing, malformed, revoked, or expired API key. Also returned when the API key lacks the required scope for the called tool.
rows.method: Unknown JSON-RPC method (e.g. calling a method other than initialize, tools/list, tools/call)
rows.param: Unknown tool name, or missing / invalid parameter in tools/call
rows.rate: Per-key rate limit or plan daily quota exceeded. Check data.error_code: "rate_limit_exceeded" vs "quota_exceeded". Check data.retry_after (seconds) before retrying.
rows.tool: Tool executed but encountered an error (inbox not found, message not found, provider auth failure, invalid recipient, attachment too large, provider 5xx). The error description is in content[0].text.

rateLimits.heading: Rate limits & quotas.
rateLimits.perKeyBody: Enforced per API key regardless of plan. When exceeded, the server returns error code -32029 with data.error_code: "rate_limit_exceeded" and a data.retry_after field (seconds). Respect that value before retrying.
rateLimits.planHeading: Free 60 / min · Solo 300 / min · Team 1,000 / min
rateLimits.planBody: Usage is unlimited; this is a per-workspace fair-use burst limit (aggregated across all your API keys). When exceeded, calls return data.error_code: "rate_limit_exceeded" with data.window: "per_minute" and a data.retry_after countdown (seconds). Upgrade your plan for a higher ceiling.
rateLimits.retryHeading: Always honour retry_after; never retry sends blindly
rateLimits.retryBody: For rate_limit_exceeded errors, wait data.retry_after seconds before retrying. Use exponential backoff for provider_error. Do not auto-retry email_compose sends on provider_error, since the message may have already been accepted by the provider.

cta.heading: Ready to connect your inbox?
cta.sub: Start on the Free plan: unlimited, no card required. Upgrade to Solo or Team for higher burst limits and team features.

meta.title: Provider Support
meta.description: See which email providers MCPEmails supports and which features are available per provider: Gmail, Fastmail, iCloud, Yahoo, Zoho, Yandex, and Generic IMAP.

hero.heading: What works, per provider.
hero.lead: MCPEmails connects Gmail, Fastmail, and any IMAP inbox (iCloud, Yahoo, Zoho, Yandex, generic). Not every provider exposes the same APIs — this table shows exactly what each one supports today.

legend.imapNote: Fastmail, iCloud, Yahoo, Zoho, Yandex, and Generic IMAP all connect over the same IMAP/SMTP transport (Fastmail and iCloud use an app-specific password) and share an identical feature set, including IMAP search syntax. The columns are shown separately for clarity.

notes.gmail: Gmail — folders vs labels: Gmail uses a flat label system rather than hierarchical folders. "Move" is implemented as label add/remove. Native copy is not available via the Gmail REST API.
notes.permanentDelete: Permanent delete: Gmail moves to Trash when you delete — permanent expunge is not exposed by their APIs. IMAP providers (Fastmail, iCloud, Yahoo, Zoho, Yandex, Generic) support both trash and hard expunge.
notes.contacts_db: Contact search (live scan): All providers support contact_search, which finds matching correspondents with a live, header-only scan of a recent window of your matching mail. There is no contacts table — nothing is stored between calls, and counts reflect only matched messages in the scanned window.
notes.scheduling: Scheduling: Supported for all providers via a server-side scheduled_sends queue. Use the schedule tool's create, list, and cancel actions. Delivery uses each provider's existing send path — no provider-native scheduling API is required.
notes.signatures: Signatures: A per-inbox signature is appended server-side on every send, reply, forward, draft, and scheduled message — this works on all providers. Set it from the dashboard per-inbox editor or the signature MCP tool, and use signature_reply_mode to control whether it appears on replies and forwards. Per call, pass include_signature: false on email_compose or draft to skip it.

cta.heading: Ready to connect your inbox?
cta.sub: Free plan: unlimited connections, no card required.
